planting.note: Plant dormant bare-root bushes in autumn or very early spring, setting the crown slightly deeper than it grew in the nursery row to encourage new basal shoots.

directions: Baldwin is a long-established English black currant long valued for its small, intensely flavored, deep black berries with exceptionally high vitamin C content, and it was one of the principal cultivars behind commercial black currant juice production in Britain. The compact, upright bush ripens its crop over a concentrated late-season window, which suits once-over hand or mechanical harvest. It is more susceptible to American gooseberry mildew and reversion virus than newer Ben-series releases, so good air circulation and clean certified stock matter. Renew about a quarter of the oldest wood each winter to keep young, productive canes coming from the base.
sources: East Malling Research historical cultivar records

planting.note: Plant bare-root while dormant in fall or early spring in cool, humus-rich soil; this far-northern selection appreciates a site that stays evenly moist through summer.

directions: Ojebyn is a traditional Scandinavian black currant, named for the village of Oujebyn in northern Sweden, selected over generations for reliable cropping and flavor under short, cool growing seasons. It produces large, strongly aromatic berries in long strigs and tolerates far colder winters than most commercial English or Dutch cultivars. Because it flowers relatively early, choose a site that avoids the worst spring frost pockets, or be ready to cover blossoms during cold nights. Thin out the oldest third of the wood each winter to keep the bush renewing itself with vigorous young canes.
sources: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) fruit breeding records

planting.note: Plant bare-root bushes while dormant in autumn or early spring, burying the crown a couple of inches deeper than it stood in the nursery row to push up new basal shoots.

directions: Laxton's Giant is a historic English black currant bred by the Laxton Brothers nursery, selected above all for producing some of the largest berries of any black currant cultivar of its era. It ripens early, which gives home growers first pick of the black currant season but also means the open flowers are more exposed to late spring frost. The bush is vigorous and spreading rather than compact, so give it generous spacing and room for air to move through the canopy to limit mildew. Remove the oldest quarter of the wood each winter, since the biggest berries form on younger one- and two-year-old stems.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society historical fruit cultivar records

planting.note: Plant bare-root currants while dormant in fall or early spring, and train as a single-stemmed bush or short standard so the drooping fruit strigs hang clear of the soil.

directions: Victoria is a long-grown English red currant valued for its reliable, heavy crops of bright red berries borne in long, loosely strung strigs late in the currant season, after earlier cultivars like Red Lake have finished. The vigorous, upright bush tolerates the partial shade of a north-facing wall better than most fruiting shrubs, making it a traditional choice for cooler corners of the kitchen garden. Its late ripening window extends the fresh red currant harvest and spreads out jelly- and cordial-making over more weeks. Prune in winter to an open goblet shape, cutting new growth back to encourage short fruiting spurs along the older framework.

planting.note: Plant bare-root while dormant in fall or early spring in fertile, moisture-retentive soil, and stake young bushes loosely until the root system establishes.

directions: Rote Riesentraube, German for 'red giant grape,' is a classic Central European heirloom red currant prized for its exceptionally long, loosely hung strigs of mild, sweet-tart berries that resemble small grape clusters. It is a dependable, self-fertile mid-season cropper that has remained popular in home orchards across Germany and neighboring countries for well over a century. The open, arching habit sheds excess moisture readily, which helps keep foliage diseases in check in humid summers. Prune out some of the oldest wood each winter and shorten overly long laterals to keep fruiting spurs close to the main framework.
sources: German pomological society (Pomologen-Verein) heirloom fruit records

planting.note: Plant bare-root bushes while dormant in fall or early spring, choosing an open-centered training shape that lets light and air reach the thorny interior branches.

directions: Catherina is a German dessert gooseberry noted for its large, amber-red, thin-skinned berries that sweeten fully if left on the bush until fully colored, making it one of the better gooseberries for eating fresh out of hand rather than cooking. The bush is vigorous and productive, with a spreading habit that benefits from a sturdy framework of main branches to support heavy fruit loads. Harvest in two passes where possible, picking the earliest-coloring berries for fresh eating and leaving the rest to size up further for jam or pie use. Keep the center of the bush open with annual winter pruning to reduce powdery mildew in humid climates.
